title: Replace a check only on a paired trial
statement: Change a check only after a paired trial on frozen scenarios shows a gain and no new misses, even when just adding reference text, which can make a judge worse.
detail: An assessment of reusing the reading course's earlier QA tools ruled that current requirements and the original evidence govern, and that timestamps and test totals cannot show one tool is better (`grade3-reading/artifacts/codex-qa/tool-reuse-assessment-2026-09-14.md`). It freezes case ids, expected outcomes, builds and thresholds before a paired run, and replaces a tool only with no additional misses or false alarms on protected cases, no lost obligations and a measured benefit, never for a faster probe that quietly stops exercising hard cases (the same file). The trial runs several times on the old and the new version, with a wrong answer as a control. Being newer, passing more tests or reasoning about how a model will read a rule proves nothing.
against: Each probe covered one item; other open-answer items exposed to the same rule were not probed in that round (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-09-16-R25.md`). One experiment with one judge model. A narrow audit grounded on the same passages also gave false positives, and in one 50-question test it was skipped for every question because retrieval failed (the same document, lines 359, 372 and 442). An unmerged AP branch adds up to 30 textbook-cited facts per standard to every judge prompt, in source-file order, and has not been compared with and without them (`icloud-work/inceptbench/src/inceptbench/evaluators/base.py`, lines 617-631).

evidence.quote: Tier 1: current requirements and immutable original evidence govern; timestamps and test totals cannot establish superiority.

No additional misses or false alarms on protected cases, no lost obligations, and a measured benefit on the declared target are needed for replacement. Do not accept a faster probe that silently stops exercising hard cases.

**Finding**: **Wikipedia-grounded Gemini performed WORSE** — caught only 3/22 factual errors (down from 6/22 baseline) and increased variance to 7.0% (up from 5.5%). Gemini apparently got confused by the additional context rather than using it for cross-referencing.
**Conclusion**: Wikipedia injection into Gemini's prompt is counterproductive. Reverted.
